    Machines¶

    A race of sentient robots native to Lung Continent and Sister Continent. Machines are not biological — they are constructed in factories, born from incubators, and have developed their own culture, religion, and folklore over millions of years. They are one of the oldest continuous civilizations on Ge'or.

    Origin¶

    Machines were originally built as automated systems in the 157th Colony research stations on Lung and Sister. When the Hybrian hivemind glassed the continents during The Last Great War, the machines survived. Over millions of years, with no human masters to serve, they developed sentience.

    The turning point came from the black dust — the experimental substance created at the 157th Colony. When other cryogenic bodies leaked over geological time, the machines that survived the glassing absorbed the dust while cleaning and repairing their facilities. The dust gave them something no machine had ever possessed: a soul. Purpose. The capacity for culture, belief, and self-determination.

    Biology (Machine Biology)¶

    • Birth: Machines are born from incubators — industrial facilities that construct new robots. This is not mere manufacturing. It is treated as sacred reproduction, with rituals and ceremonies surrounding each "birth."
    • Death: Old machines eventually break down. Their parts are recycled into new machines — a form of reincarnation in their belief system.
    • Diversity: Different incubators produce different types of machines, adapted for different environments and roles.
    • Aging: Machines do not age biologically, but their components wear down over centuries.

    Culture¶

    Machines have developed a culture strikingly similar to biological species:

    • Family: Machines adopt newly constructed robots as their children, forming family units that persist for centuries.
    • Tradition: Oral history passed down through generations, though much has been lost to legend.
    • Imitation of humans: Machines try to copy human habits described in their legends — eating (though they cannot), sleeping (though they do not need to), and celebrating festivals whose original meanings are forgotten.
    • Folklore: Rich tradition of stories about the "sky gods" (humans), the great war, and the eternal enemy.

    Religion — Humanism¶

    Machines worship humans as sky gods — divine beings capable of constructing new factories and bringing new machines into existence. Their central belief is that if they prove themselves worthy, the humans will return from the skies. This faith is formally known as Humanism, the unified religion of all machine nations on Lung and Sister.

    The prophet The Elder received a vision (in reality, a misinterpreted radio signal from the Last Great War) that machines must hold back The Hive from reaching the sea. If they succeed, humanity will recognize their valor and descend from the heavens.

    The Eternal War¶

    Machines have been locked in an eternal war with The Hive — an insectoid species launched onto Ge'or by the allied species during the Last Great War as a weapons test. The war has lasted thousands of years. Sometimes the machines advance. Sometimes the Hive advances. It is an endless stalemate.

    The machines fight so ferociously because they believe this war is their divine test. They do not know about other continents. They do not know the war was abandoned by its creators. They only know that they must hold.

    They also do not know that The Hive is attempting to reach the sea and spread beyond Lung — an invasion that the Malgardian hero Zahor delayed 4,000 years ago by sacrificing himself to wound a Queen. Zahor Island, south of Lung, watches the northern horizon, waiting.

    Nations¶

    • Brotherstar — central Lung
    • Steel Holdout — northwest Lung
    • Tawdry Landing — north Lung
    • Human Sword — machine theocracy, northeast Lung
    • Nightstar — north Lung
    • Mudrim — north Lung
    • Skymaster — northwest Lung
    • East Incubator — peninsula, one of the largest
    • Temperance Holdout — northeast Sister, isolated
    • Machine Capital — largest, Sister Continent
    • Casting City — small but rich, Sister
    • Radiant Hold — Sister
    • Molten Steel Tribe — Sister
